name: reload-chords
description:
the four reload strengths, driven as real chords at a page that can say which one it got.

WHAT THE PAGE MEASURES. reload-probe.html reads three things on every load. `loads` is a localStorage counter, so it survives an ordinary reload and resets only when the site's data is cleared. `cookie` is 'kept' when the page found its own cookie already set and 'fresh' when it had to set it again, which is the same signal read the other way round. `css` is the verdict on its own stylesheet, taken from PerformanceResourceTiming: transferSize 0 is a cache hit, transferSize below encodedBodySize is a 304 that moved headers only, and transferSize at or above encodedBodySize is the body coming back over the wire. The harness serves the fixtures with python3 -m http.server, which sends Last-Modified and no Cache-Control, so an ordinary reload revalidates and only a cache-bypassing one refetches. The verdict is therefore a byte-threshold-free read: nothing here depends on how big the stylesheet happens to be.

WHY A REAL CHORD AND NOT atriumSetNavModifiers. A sibling scenario drives the sidebar button's modifier ladder through the JS receiver because a HELD modifier state has to persist across a redraw and cgevent cannot hold and release cleanly. These are one-shot presses, which send_combo does deliver - a sibling scenario already presses cmd+r this way - so the keyboard path itself is what is under test here, not a simulation of it.

THE RED THIS RECORDED, measured on the build of 2026-09-07. Atrium's core hotkey table ships no reload action, so all four chords fall through to whatever Chromium's own menu binds: accelerators_cocoa.mm binds Cmd+R to IDC_RELOAD and Cmd+Shift+R to IDC_RELOAD_BYPASSING_CACHE, and nothing at all binds Cmd+Option+R or Cmd+Option+Shift+R. The counter went 1, 2, 3, 3 - Cmd+R reloaded and served the stylesheet from cache, Cmd+Shift+R reloaded and refetched it, and the last two chords did nothing whatever.

VACUITY GUARD, once per rung. A chord that never arrives leaves the previous load's verdict in window.probe, and 'network' left over from Cmd+Shift+R is indistinguishable from 'network' earned by Cmd+Option+R. The loads counter is the only read that tells those apart, which is why every rung has one - the first version of this scenario did not, and it scored rungs 3 and 4 as passing on a page nobody had reloaded.

actions.note: GATE: the probe really committed as the startup tab before any chord is pressed
an ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot, and every chord below would land in Finder
BASELINE: first load of a clean profile, so the counter starts at 1 and every later read is against a known floor
ReloadType::NORMAL revalidates the main resource only, so the stylesheet is served straight from cache and transfers nothing
VACUITY GUARD for this rung: a chord that never reloaded leaves the previous load's verdict standing, which reads exactly like a correct answer
a hard reload is not a site-data wipe - the cookie has to survive this rung, or rung 4 proves nothing
RUNG 3, empty the cache and hard reload
VACUITY GUARD, and the one that records the reported bug: on today's build Cmd+Option+R is bound to nothing and this stays at 3
emptying the HTTP cache is not emptying the site's storage, so the cookie stands here too
RUNG 4, clear this site's cookies and site data, then hard reload
the removal is asynchronous and the reload waits on its reply, so this rung settles longer than the three above
localStorage went with the cookies, so the counter is back at its first-load value

assertions.desc: sanity: one real window throughout, so no chord opened or closed one
assertions.label: one-window-still

assertions.desc: BASELINE: the probe loaded once on a clean profile
THE VACUITY GUARD. Cmd+R reloaded the page it was pressed at. Every css read below is worthless if this fails, because an unpressed chord and a wrong reload look identical in the cache verdict.
AC: Cmd+R is the ordinary reload - it revalidates the page and serves the stylesheet from cache
VACUITY GUARD for rung 2: the chord reloaded the page, so the cache verdict beside it is this load's and not the last one's
Cmd+Shift+R reloads past the cache, so the stylesheet body comes back over the wire
Cmd+Shift+R is a cache bypass and nothing more - the site's cookie is untouched

THE REPORTED BUG, stated as one number. On today's build Cmd+Option+R is bound to nothing at all and this reads 3 - the page never reloaded, and the cache verdict below is the previous chord's answer left standing.
Cmd+Option+R empties the cache and reloads, so the body is fetched again
Emptying the cache leaves the site's cookies alone, which is what separates rung 3 from rung 4
Cmd+Option+Shift+R cleared the site's cookies before reloading, so the page had to set its own again
LocalStorage went with the cookies. Cookies alone would leave this counter climbing, so this is the half that proves the whole of the site's data went.
Cmd+Q still quits cleanly after four reloads and a site-data removal
